Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Attaching our SOC 2 Type II report and a current subprocessor roster to start: see attachments. A few quick points to address your questions below; I can provide a short attestation PDF as well (attached) that you can upload to your portal.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025.pdf (PDF); redwood-subprocessors-2025.csv (CSV); redwood-carveout-attestation-2025.pdf (PDF)

Short answers:
- Audit period: Our SOC 2 Type II covers controls tested from 2024-03-01 through 2025-02-28 (we call this the 2024 coverage year in the report).
- Cloud provider model: Redwood's SOC 2 report is issued with a carve-out for third-party data center/physical security controls and infrastructure-level controls performed by our cloud providers. In other words, we treat cloud providers (e.g., AWS, GCP) as subservice organizations under a carve-out model. That means the cloud provider's controls are not included in Redwood's test population; we rely on the cloud provider's own SOC reports and certifications for those controls.
- Bridge letters / attestations: We do not control AWS/GCP's issuance of bridge letters. Where feasible we provide a Redwood attestation that references the cloud provider SOC 2 reports that Redwood relies on and confirms how those responsibilities map to our control set. We have an internal attestation attached (redwood-carveout-attestation-2025.pdf). If your team requires a formal bridge letter from AWS/GCP, we can provide guidance on requesting that from the provider, but AWS/GCP typically publish their SOC reports to customer consoles rather than issuing bespoke bridge letters.
- Subprocessors: The attached CSV lists subprocessors and high-level functions (logging, storage, key management). Please note that key management for customer-managed keys is optional; by default Redwood manages KMS keys for hosted deployments. We can provide tenant-specific details if you have a contract or PO in place.

If it's helpful I can follow up with a short note that maps each cloud responsibility (network, compute, physical, hypervisor) to Redwood controls for your vendor risk template.

Best,
